facts.text: Trailing-twelve-month revenue is ₹3.60 lakh cr, +4% on the prior twelve months.
Trailing-twelve-month PAT is ₹83,685 cr, +12% on the prior twelve months.
Sep 2026 quarter: revenue ₹95,132 cr (+9% YoY), PAT ₹21,537 cr (+6% YoY).
Revenue has compounded at 19% over 10 years, 22% over 5 and 27% over 3; the last twelve months (+4%) are running behind the 3-year pace.
Profit has compounded slower than revenue over 3 years (18% vs 27%).
Quarterly revenue growth has accelerated over the last four quarters: +2% → +0% → +4% → +9% YoY.
Deposits stand at ₹33.24 lakh cr, +7% since Mar 2026.
Assets are 8.6× shareholders' equity (₹6.03 lakh cr); leverage is the business model for a lender, so watch asset quality rather than debt.
Foreign institutions hold 39.4%, −9.0 pp over a year.
Operating cash flow is not a useful quality test for a lender — deposits and loans flow through it. Judge earnings quality on asset quality and provisioning instead.

claims.claim: Management believes the net interest margin trajectory will be upward from the next quarter onwards.
claims.quote: The trajectory will be upward from the next quarter onwards.

claims.claim: Management claims Q2 FY27 margins represent the bottom for the bank.
claims.quote: Yes, by all account, Parag, that is what we were alluding to, to say that the rate cycle having already kicked in earlier in October, that is a good tailwind

claims.claim: The bank's liquidity position is described as extremely comfortable.
claims.quote: the institution's liquidity is extremely comfortable and probably slightly more than comfortable.

claims.claim: The bank sees significant opportunity to gain market share in over 54% of the 765 districts it operates in.
claims.quote: out of the 765 districts that we are in, more than 54% of the districts, significant opportunity exists because we are 2 to 3 percentage points lower than our average market share

claims.claim: The bank's asset quality remains pristine with GNPA at 1.11%.
claims.quote: Our asset quality remains pristine, with GNPA at 1.11%, 13 basis points lower than year-on-year.

claims.claim: The bank continues to gain market share in deposits on both an incremental and stock basis.
claims.quote: We continue to gain market share both on an incremental basis and on a stock basis as well.

claims.claim: There is healthy credit demand in the system.
claims.quote: There is a very healthy credit demand that we are seeing in the system as we speak.

claims.claim: The bank expects cost of funds to moderate as maturity of borrowings and growth play out.
claims.quote: the maturity should take care of that to some extent and the overall growth should also take care of it to the balance of the extent

claims.claim: The bank expects to see a step up in unit economics and healthy growth over the next 1-3 years.
claims.quote: my hunch tells me that I think you should see reasonably healthy growth over a one, two, three-year period in the savings account as well.

claims.claim: The bank has seen strong disbursement growth in MSME, wheels, and unsecured segments.
claims.quote: We've also continued to see very good growth come in our MSME segment... We've also similarly seen a strong growth in our unsecured business

claims.claim: The bank has gained market share on deposits every year, almost around 30 to 50 basis points over the last 5 years.
claims.quote: We have demonstrated our ability to gain market share on deposits every year, almost around 30 to 50 basis points over the last 5 years.

claims.claim: The bank is the number one MSME bank in the country, leading in 15 out of 28 states.
claims.quote: today, we are number one in the country on the entire SME space—or MSME space. And to give you some granularity, we are number one in 15 out of 28 states

claims.claim: The bank's return on assets remained stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies.
claims.quote: Despite the drop in NIMs, the return on assets continue to be stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies

claims.claim: The bank holds 35% to 40% of capital market account settlements and 40% to 50% of escrow settlements.
claims.quote: In the Capital Markets segment, we continue to hold about 35% to 40% of the account settlements. In the bankers to issue we hold about 40% to 50% of the escrow settlement.

claims.claim: The bank has a provisioning buffer of 125 basis points to absorb future shocks.
claims.quote: The bank has created a large provisioning buffer of almost 125 basis points to absorb any shocks in the future

claims.claim: The bank has 6% of the country's branch network but 11% of the market share of deposits.
claims.quote: currently, we have only a little more than 6% of the country's branch network with us. So that means our branches 9,600 plus is about a little more than 6% of the systems branch, right. And we have more than 11% of the market share of deposits with us.

claims.claim: The bank's cost of funds decreased by approximately 10-11 basis points during the quarter.
claims.quote: If you look at our cost of funds is down by about 10 basis points, 11 basis points or so in the quarter.

claims.claim: New branches contribute slightly over 20% of the bank's incremental deposits.
claims.quote: on an incremental basis, when you look at it, these new branches contribute slightly north of 20% of the overall incremental deposits that come

claims.claim: NIM compressed by 8 basis points due to front-loading of interest rate cuts on the asset side.
claims.quote: As expected, due to the front loading of the interest rate cuts on the asset side of the balance sheet, we did see NIM compress by about 8 basis points.

claims.claim: The bank continues to see market share gains in deposits.
claims.quote: We continue to see market share gains in deposits and we are very focused and disciplined in pricing.

claims.claim: The bank added approximately Rs 1,600 crores in contingent provisions during the quarter.
claims.quote: at an aggregate level, the contingent provisions have been added by about Rs.1,600 crores or so.

claims.claim: The bank has reduced turnaround time for home loan sanctions to two days for salaried and three days for self-employed.
claims.quote: For salaried loans, we have now brought down the turnaround time to two days and for self-employed, it is about three days.

claims.claim: Quarterly fluctuations in margins are expected due to the lead-lag impact of rate changes on assets versus liabilities.
claims.quote: Whilst we may see quarterly fluctuations in margins due to this lead lag impact, we expect to stabilize it over a period of time.

claims.claim: The bank is seeing healthy demand from the rural side and expects festive season impetus to boost urban consumption.
claims.quote: So we are seeing some amount of healthy demand from the rural side. I think the segment which we are catering to is already factoring in better monsoon.

claims.claim: The bank grew average deposits at 16% year-on-year and continued to gain market share.
claims.quote: Last year, we have grown our average deposits at a healthy pace of 16% year-on-year and continued to gain market share as we have done in the past.

claims.claim: The bank successfully reduced its credit-deposit ratio from 110% at the time of merger to about 95%.
claims.quote: we slowed down our average advances or AUM assets under management growth to about 7% last year in alignment with our strategic objectives to bring down the CD / credit deposit ratio from 110% at the time of merger to about 95% as we speak today.

claims.claim: The bank's asset side is 70% floating rate, while the liability side is more fixed, creating a headwind during downward rate cycles.
claims.quote: a large part of our asset side of the balance sheet is floating in nature. It's somewhere around the 70%, and whilst the liability side is more or less fixed in nature.

synthesis.one_liner: Revenue growth is recovering to 9.4% YoY, but LTM expansion of 4% trails historical compounding as margins remain under scrutiny.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management targets outperforming system credit growth in FY27 while gaining district-level market share.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Quarterly revenue growth accelerated to 9.4% YoY in Sep 2026, though LTM growth of 4% lags 27% 3-year CAGR.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management claims Q2 FY27 margins mark the bottom and NIM will trend upward from next quarter.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Sep 2026 PAT grew only 5.8% YoY to ₹21,537 cr, while 3-year profit growth (18%) lags revenue (27%).

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Management claims continuous market share gains in deposits and targets pre-merger CASA levels around 38%.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Deposits reached ₹33.24 lakh cr, up 7% over the six months since Mar 2026.

synthesis.credibility: All 9 guidance items are unmeasured against headline financials. Management frequently deflected analyst questions regarding NIM trajectory, branch expansion sufficiency, cost ratios, and credit costs.

bull.evidence: Revenue YoY growth accelerated over four quarters from 2% to 9.4% in Sep 2026.
Deposits grew 7% since Mar 2026 to reach ₹33.24 lakh cr.
Trailing-twelve-month PAT rose 12% YoY to ₹83,685 cr.

bear.evidence: Trailing twelve-month revenue growth of 4% trails the 3-year CAGR of 27%.
Profit compounded at 18% over 3 years, behind revenue growth of 27%.
Foreign institutional holding dropped 9.0 percentage points YoY to 39.4%.

watch: Movement in credit-deposit ratio toward the 85% to 90% target range.
Rebound in net interest margin following the claimed Q2 FY27 bottom.
Deposit CASA ratio progress toward the 38% pre-merger target.
